main_text.l: prudentia, nec in causa bonitas, nec
crudelitas in poena; quæ sub Nerone
tanta fuit, vt Christiani illum propterea
Antichristum putauerint, referente Au-
gustino lib. 20. de ciuit. Dei, ca. 19. [Quæ
enim poenarum genera, inquit{e} Gre-
gorius, nouimus, quæ non tum vires
“Martyrum exercuisse gaudemus, ali-
os namq; improuiso ictu immersus
iugulo gladius strauit, alios crucis pa-
tibulum affixit, in quo & mors prouo-
cata repelitur, & repulsa prouocatur”
alios hirsutis Serra dentibus attriuit,
alios armato ferro insulcans vngula
sparsit, alios belluina rabies morsibus”
detruncando comminuit, alios ab in-
timis viscerum per cutem pressa vis
verberum rupit, alios effossa terra vi-
uentes operuit, alios ab alto dimissos
in mortem præcipitium fregit, alios
in se proiectos aqua replenda obsor-
buit, alios denique edax flamma vsq;
ad cineres depasta consumpsit.] Quin
imo ipse Tacitus equestri loco Romæ
natus, & sub Vespasiano Procurator da-
tus Galliæ Belgicæ, lib. 15. Annal. affir-
mat, [Abolendo rumori de Roma“

page.notes: Quotation marks at line ends follow the printed “ and ” as set. Brackets [ ] are printed in the text and kept. The reference mark e is printed as a small superscript after "inquit" and is marked here as {e}. The quotation in the text ends mid-sentence at the foot of the page and continues on the next page.
